messages:
sarah: Customer (Acme) reporting intermittent \"invalid JSON\" errors when they call our API with response_format=json & strict mode enabled. They see 406/415 and sometimes 200 but parser fails.

sarah: Repro curl:
```
curl -v -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer xxxxx\" \
  -H \"Accept: application/json\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\",\"response_format\":\"json\",\"strict\":true}'
```

sarah: Customer says it is intermittent, more frequent under load spikes. Attached trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d
sarah: Sample raw response they captured (trimmed):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

<html><head>...</head><body>error</body></html>
```

sarah: But customer also saw this other case where content-type=application/json but extra bytes appended: `...}\n\n<!-- powered by nginx -->`

mike: Can you paste the exact trace id and a full raw capture (including headers + bytes)? sounds like negotiation bug or upstream error page leaking through when strict mode enforces JSON parsing.

sarah: trace: trace-0a1b2c3d
sarah: raw capture uploaded to inc-attachments/1718004321/trace-0a1b2c3d.txt

julia: Workaround: ask customer to set `strict=false` or add header `X-Redwood-Accept: application/json` to force our negotiator to prefer json. Not ideal but reduces failures.

eng-oncall: FYI I saw a related regression yesterday after we merged PR 0f3e1b -> changed Accept precedence in ingress. Rolling back might help. I'll check negotiator logs around trace id.

ops-bot: deploy 2026-03-05T12:03Z rolled to prod (ingress-negotiator v2.14.1)

mike: If they are on Dedicated, we might need to check their reverse proxy (customer side) because upstream 502/html could be coming from their backend during auth refresh. But the `extra trailing HTML` case suggests a chunked framing bug where trailing bytes are not stripped.

sarah: Customer is on Dedicated (tenant acme-prod). They confirm they run a Nginx 1.20 sidecar. They will try to disable gzip/chunked and retest. Asked for instruction for us to look at ingress logs for that tenant.

mike: Escalating to eng-runtime. Please collect: full raw capture (include chunk boundaries), request-id header returned, ingress/negotiator logs for tenant acme-prod around timestamp 1718004200-1718004400. Marking this P1 for now since it causes broken production for customer.

julia: Noted. I told customer we'll try the workaround and asked for ETA. Opening support ticket SUP-4791 and linking trace.

sarah: Thanks. I pushed a quick policy to allow `text/html` body if it parses as JSON (dangerous) as temporary mitigation for this tenant — please coordinate rollback once we have root cause.

eng-oncall: Please don't enable that global. For the tenant-specific mitigation it's OK temporarily. I'll pull the negotiator traces now.

mike: Adding a unit test for chunked trailing bytes and HTTP content-negotiation to catch regression. Will follow up in SUP-4791 and eng ticket RT-2127.

sarah: Customer will test and update. I'll post results here.
